ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass via SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96() overflow
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, but AMMStandardHook._validatePricingBounds checks sqrtPriceX96 == 0 and reverts with AMMStandardHook__InvalidPrice (line 847-849). DynamicPoolType uses default price limits (MIN_SQRT_RATIO+1 / MAX_SQRT_RATIO-1) when swapExtraData is not 32 bytes. No path to zero-price swap.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call bypassing pricing enforcement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer (line 230) and PermitTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer (line 115) both check msg.sender != AMM and revert. CLOBTransferHandler.afterSwapRefund (line 316) also checks msg.sender == AMM. AMMStandardHook.beforeSwap/afterSwap use _requireCallerIsAMM. No path to bypass.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap between CLOBTransferHandler and CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: setTokenSettings is admin-only (requireCallerIsTokenOrContractOwnerOrAdminOrRole, line 273). Token settings are read fresh from storage at swap time (AMMModule lines 1356, 1369, 1519, 1532, 1827-1828). No stale cache. Settings changes are admin-controlled, not attacker-exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak in DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known HOOK-001 issue. Slot written in beforeSwap (line 839) not cleared in afterSwap. However: (1) transient storage cleared at end of TX, (2) within TX a second direct swap overwrites slot in beforeSwap before afterSwap reads it, (3) AMM always calls beforeSwap then afterSwap sequentially. Stale value can't cause profit extraction. Informational only.

_setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at line 3190 preserves the ENTERED bit (bit 1). Only custom operation flags (SWAP_GUARD_FLAG etc) are cleared to allow collectHookFeesByHook. The ENTERED bit blocks reentrancy into all nonReentrantWithFlags-protected functions. Verified in TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags.sol.
Forge test with 100 tiny (1 wei) swaps shows attacker loses value each swap due to fees. No rounding error accumulation that benefits attacker. Pool remains solvent throughout.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Transient-slot theft: write in path A, read stale in path B
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test: two swaps in same TX, second swap's transient storage is independent. Pool remains solvent. DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT overwritten by each beforeSwap, not readable cross-swap.

Forge test: excess ETH refund triggers callback, but reentrancy guard (ENTERED bit) blocks re-entry. The refund at line 3253 uses low-level call with excess value, but all AMM entry points check reentrancy. Pool remains solvent.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forged hook caller: call hook directly with fake pool identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMStandardHook uses _requireCallerIsAMM() which checks msg.sender == AMM. CLOBTransferHandler checks msg.sender == AMM. PermitTransferHandler checks msg.sender == AMM. All hook entry points protected.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Storage-slot collision across diamond proxy facets
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Diamond storage at slot 0x9A1D. Pool types (DynamicPoolType, FixedPoolType, SingleProviderPoolType) are external contracts called via CALL (not delegatecall) — they have separate storage space. No slot collision possible between AMM facets and pool types. Verified with pool creation + swap test.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Permit mutation: replay signature with mutated feeOnTop fields
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop is intentionally NOT signed in SWAP_TYPEHASH (known design). Executor sets feeOnTop for integrator revenue share. Signer protected by limitAmount (signed) which caps minimum output. Cosigner provides additional off-chain validation. No path to profit beyond what signer authorized.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: CLOB settlement callback reads stale AMM state mid-swap
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer operates on its own orderBook state, not AMM reserves. Called AFTER pool reserves are updated (lines 1436-1443). Has nonReentrant guard. Cannot re-enter AMM or observe stale reserves.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: View function stale read during callback enables arbitrage
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: getPoolState reads directly from storage. During swap execution, reserves are updated atomically before afterSwap hooks. Any callback sees consistent state for that point in execution. Reentrancy guard prevents state-changing re-entry. No arbitrageable desync.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Sibling repo cached value leads to stale data exploitation
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool types are called synchronously during AMM swap execution via external CALL. Their state updates happen within the same call frame. No caching layer between AMM and pool type state. Forge test confirms 3 sequential swaps maintain solvency and state consistency.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Flash loan + swap round trip profit extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test (fuzzed): flash loan -> swap -> reverse swap -> repay. Attacker always loses money due to fees. No flash loan arbitrage path within a single pool. Cross-pool arbitrage also loses to fees (tested in C15/C16).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Multi-swap state not isolated between hops
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Forge test with 2-pool multi-swap path. Each pool swap updates reserves atomically. Mock hooks cannot observe cross-pool intermediate state because each pool's beforeSwap/afterSwap is called per-hop. Reentrancy guard prevents nested swaps.

theft_theses.thesis: Re-enter via transfer handler during swap to read stale reserves
Multi-swap within hook callback causes transient slot overwrite mid-swap
Native ETH refund during hook triggers reentrancy to observe intermediate state
CLOB settlement callback reads AMM state before swap finalizes
Trigger callback mid-state-update → external integrator reads stale view → arbitrage
Function A writes partial state → call function B before commit → extract inconsistency
External call to sibling repo returns cached value → stale data → profit
ETH transfer triggers 2300 gas callback → observe stale transient slot → extract
